page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU and multi-threaded decompression benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block uncached reads and writes at 46.82 GB/sec and 27.55 GB/sec respectively, while small-block cached reads are weaker. Cryptographic and text processing capabilities remain average, but database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving are relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-4 offers a high memory density per vCPU without the added cost of local NVMe storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. Appropriate workloads include medium-scale database caching, memory-intensive text processing, single-threaded application servers, and lightweight LLM text generation using small models.
